text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc's Famvir is an effective treatment for women who suffer from frequent genital herpes outbreaks, according to a study at the University of New Mexico School of Medicine.
The drug is presently used as a treatment for recurring genital herpes, but the study is to determine its effectiveness in preventing future genital herpes outbreaks, the university said.

After four months of treatment, 90 percent of the patients who were administered 250 mg of Famvir twice daily were recurrence-free compared to 48 percent of placebo-treated patients, the university said about the study that was published in the Archives of Internal Medicine.

The double-blind, placebo controlled trial was conducted at 11 universities and nine private ambulatory care referral centers to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Famvir given once or twice daily for the suppression of frequent episodes of genital herpes on women, the university said.
The university conducted the survey on 375 women with recurrent genital herpes simplex infection, it said.
The study found that the drug was more effective with two doses a day, rather than one a day.

"More frequent dosing allows the antiviral to continually circulate in the bloodstream, so there's a greater potential to stop the virus in its tracks," Dr. Gregory Mertz, the study's author, said in a statement.

In the United States, 55 million adults, or one-in-four adults, have genital herpes and approximately 500,000 new cases of genital herpes occur annually, the university said. Many herpes patients do not show signs of exhibiting the herpes virus, a spokeswoman for the university said.
The study was supported by a clinical grant from SmithKline Beecham, the university said.
